newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced on relatively high volume on Tuesday morning with a good portion of market activity focused on China-related new listings, brokers said.
"Once we took out the stale bulls, the market was ready to go higher," said a trader with a large U.S. house. "There were just too many longs in this market."
The Hang Seng Index was 61 points higher at 13,330, edging up from an open of 13,304. Turnover was high at HK$3.16 billion after 40 minutes of trade.
Investors were also encouraged by the strong rally on Wall Street, the U.S. broker added.
The Dow industrials rose 78.50 points, or 1.12 percent, to close at an all-time closing high of 7,079.39
Some caution was seen in the bond market, where the U.S. 30-year long bond ended down 1/32 at 97-17/32 to yield 6.82 percent, unchanged from Friday.
Red chips, H shares and small and mid-cap issues outperformed the blue chip index.
"Stocks with landbanks of inexpensive China property will be a new focus of the market," said Charles Cheung at J&A Securities.
Shenzhen-based Shum Yip Investment gained HK$0.55 to HK$5.85 in early trade, then eased to trade HK$0.20 higher at HK$5.50.
H share newcomer China Eastern rose to a new high of HK$2.50, then inched back to trade HK$0.075 higher at HK$2.40. Brokers said they expected the issue to rise to HK$4.00 within 12 months.
The mid-cap index was trading 1.04 percent higher compared to the Hang Seng's gain of 0.39 percent.
Leading the sector was Dah Sing with a jump of HK$1.20 to HK$32.00. The company posted a 26.5 percent rise in 1996 earnings on Monday.
Among the blue chips, Hutchison Whampoa advanced HK$0.75 to HK$58.25.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings added gained HK$1.00 to HK$191.00 and subsidiary Hang Seng Bank put on HK$0.25 to HK84.50.
Hang Seng Index futures continued to drag on the market, brokers said.
The March contract was trading 67 points higher at 13,292, but still at a discount to the cash market.
